title: Ensemble-dependent effect of disorder on multicritical points in a system with long-range interactions
abstract: We introduce two variants of the Blume--Emery--Griffiths model with long-range, mean-field-like interactions and quenched disorder. Although the two variants are described by different Hamiltonians, they yield the same free energy. Moreover, both Hamiltonians lead to the same average energy and hence to the same microcanonical entropy. The canonical and microcanonical phase boundaries differ markedly, and so does the multicritical behaviour of the two ensembles. In the microcanonical ensemble, tricritical points appear for any fraction of active spins, whereas in the canonical ensemble they emerge only when this fraction is sufficiently large. At lower fractions, canonical critical endpoints arise instead. We also report the formation of gaps in the entropy as a function of magnetization, another manifestation of ensemble inequivalence.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the phase transitions in a disordered system with long-range interactions using the BEG model. It demonstrates a significant ensemble inequivalence, showing that the canonical and microcanonical descriptions predict different critical behaviors. The work provides detailed conditions for the existence of multicritical points based on the disorder strength.
main_problem: The paper investigates the ensemble-dependent effects of quenched disorder on the critical and multicritical points of a system with long-range interactions.
main_result: The canonical and microcanonical ensembles yield distinctly different phase diagrams, showing differences in the existence and nature of tricritical and critical endpoints.
method: The analysis employs both the replica trick for the canonical ensemble (calculating free energy) and direct entropy calculations for the microcanonical ensemble.
model_or_system: The study uses two variants of the Blume-Emery-Griffiths (BEG) model incorporating quenched disorder and long-range interactions, analyzed in the thermodynamic limit.
key_observables: Free energy density ($f$), entropy density ($s$), magnetization ($m$), and the location of multicritical points (CTPs, CEPs, MTPs).
important_parameters: Disorder fraction ($p$), coupling strength ($J$), crystal field ($\Delta$), and inverse temperature ($ eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the saddle point approximation and the replica symmetry ansatz for the canonical ensemble.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between canonical and microcanonical phase diagrams, showing re-entrant behavior in the canonical case and the free energy/entropy dependence on magnetization.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by introducing the two Hamiltonians, deriving the free energy and entropy potentials in terms of order parameters, and then comparing the resulting phase boundaries and critical point conditions for both ensembles.
why_interesting: The explicit comparison between canonical and microcanonical ensembles, especially regarding phase transitions and disorder effects, provides deep insight into the fundamental statistical mechanical definitions of equilibrium states, which is relevant to understanding complex many-body systems.
